answers.answer: No — 150 is not a perfect square

steps: 144 < 150 < 169, so 150 sits strictly between consecutive perfect squares.
So √150 lies strictly between 12 and 13 and is not a whole number.
Recomputed independently from the recorded parameters, the oracle returns No — 150 is not a perfect square; the option matching it is “No — 150 is not a perfect square”.
solutionReasoning.answer: No — 150 is not a perfect square

answers.answer: √81 = 9 exactly; √80 lies between 8 and 9 and has no exact whole-number value.

steps: 81 is a perfect square: 9² = 81, so √81 = 9 exactly.
80 is not: the perfect squares on either side are 8² = 64 and 9² = 81, and 64 < 80 < 81.
So √80 lies strictly between 8 and 9 and cannot be a whole number.
solutionReasoning.answer: √81 = 9 exactly; √80 lies between 8 and 9 and has no exact whole-number value.
